title: NATO makes civilian resilience part of military readiness while implementation remains open
source_unit: NATO 2026 Resilience Baseline Requirements official text
geography: NATO civil-military resilience planning and Host Nation Support requirements

whole_of_society_governance.unit: resilience planning across government and society

resource_planning.unit: reliable and sustained resource planning for resilience

civil_systems_in_scope.value: movement of people, food and water, health and mass casualties, communications, transportation, border crossing, and supply-chain/private-sector dependencies

host_nation_support.unit: civil support for allied military movement and operations

population_effect_mitigation.unit: mitigation of military and civil-plan effects on populations while maintaining essential services

national_implementation.unit: country compliance, funding, and operating performance

observations.method: Review of the official NATO 2026 Resilience Baseline Requirements text; policy requirements are kept separate from country-level implementation and outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The document establishes an alliance policy framework but does not provide country-by-country compliance, budgets, exercise results, outage data, service continuity, public opinion, or crisis performance.
observations.subgroup: NATO member and partner civil authorities, military planners, Host Nation Support actors, essential-service providers, and private-sector dependencies named by the policy.
observations.counterinterpretation: The requirements can strengthen civilian protection and essential-service continuity as well as military enablement; the policy text alone cannot show how that balance works in practice or who bears the costs.

boundary: This record captures a formal NATO policy connection between civilian resilience and military readiness. It does not establish national implementation, spending, public consent, burden distribution, essential-service performance, Host Nation Support performance, or deterrence and crisis outcomes.
